description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Access to Trade Finance for Issuing Banks and Traders: Issuing Banks (IBs) in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs) face ongoing challenges in obtaining financing for traders importing/exporting commodities, including critical goods like food and energy. IBs depend on global Confirming Banks (CBs), but CBs face limits on counterparties/geographies, higher capital reserve requirements, AML/CFT compliance, and heightened risk perceptions from recent crises. These constraints reduce CB capacity to meet IB needs.
The Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) supports IBs and their customers by providing IFC guarantees to CBs, mitigating risk and enabling trade flows that would not occur otherwise. Guarantees are vital for low-income and fragile/conflict-affected countries, where few CBs participate. GTFP allocates line limits to IBs, who draw on IFC guarantees for transactions requiring CB coverage. By definition, each GTFP transaction would not have happened without IFC, and collectively they sustain EMDE trade and GDP. IFCs presence helps IBs maintain, expand, and strengthen correspondent banking networks, connect with new banks, and gain trade finance experience.
Market Creation Integration: GTFP enhances market integration by: (1) maintaining/expanding trade finance, linkages, and trade across markets via stronger bilateral correspondent connections; (2) serving as a platform for new localinternational bank and customer connections; and (3) channeling new capital to EMDE trade through demonstration and replication of successful models. This network is critical to sustaining finance in markets facing cross-border retrenchment, making GTFP IFCs entry point to new banking relationships, even in challenging countries, due to the low-risk nature of trade finance assets.

The proposed project is an unfunded trade finance facility under IFCs Global Trade Finance Program (GTFP) of up to US$30 million for Banco BBVA Argentina S.A (BBVA Argentina or the Bank). The trade line will support the Banks short-term trade finance transactions by offering confirming banks partial or full guarantees to cover payment risk of the Bank in Argentina.
